issues.issue: The litigation representation carves out "litigation with respect to which pleadings or documents have been filed with a court, but not served on the Master Servicer" and is further qualified by a "reasonable likelihood of resulting in a material adverse effect", neither of which has any stated measure. What must be disclosed is therefore left to argument.

The survival sentence says the representations survive "any termination of the Master Servicer hereunder" without any time limit or reference to the successor-servicer provisions of Article VI and VII. Its reach against a replaced Master Servicer must be worked out against those provisions.

Section 2.08 lets the Indenture Trustee enforce the Sponsor's repurchase obligations "without joinder of the Depositor or the Issuing Entity", while Section 2.03(a) provides that the Depositor shall take enforcement actions at the request of the Issuing Entity or Indenture Trustee and reserves certain enforcement rights to the Sponsor. Which party may sue the Sponsor, and whether the Note Insurer may, is answerable only by reading the two sections together.

The same Section obliges the Master Servicer to monitor, reconcile and coordinate corrective adjustments to the Servicer's records and then states that it "shall be entitled to conclusively rely on the HELOC data provided to it by the Servicer and shall have no liability for any errors in such HELOC data". The duty to detect errors and the immunity for errors cannot both be given full effect.

This paragraph obliges the Indenture Trustee to furnish powers of attorney with no precondition, while Section 4.04 conditions the same duty on "written request from a Servicing Officer" and on conformity with Accepted Master Servicing Practices. Whether a request must come from a Servicing Officer depends on which of the two overlapping provisions controls.

This paragraph requires the Master Servicer, Securities Administrator and Indenture Trustee to provide records access and photocopying "at a charge that covers ... actual costs", while Section 4.07(a) requires the same access to information and documentation regarding the HELOCs to be "afforded without charge". The two cannot both govern the same request.

The Indenture Trustee must execute "any court pleadings, requests for trustee's sale or other documents necessary or reasonably desirable" for the listed enforcement steps, a catch-all whose reach beyond the four enumerated purposes is undefined, especially against clause (iv)'s open-ended "any other rights or remedies ... otherwise available at law or equity". What the Trustee can be compelled to sign is left unbounded.

Section 4.02(a) leaves termination of the Servicer to the Master Servicer's own "judgment" and permits it to "take such other action as it deems appropriate", while Section 4.02(b) imposes a mandatory duty to enforce and to terminate on a failure to perform, subject to the Note Insurer's prior written consent. Whether termination is discretionary or mandatory, and whether consent is required, turns on reading the two subsections together.

The subsection first conditions any termination of the Servicer on the Note Insurer's prior written consent, then adds a proviso that "if the Servicer has failed to make any payment such that the Master Servicer had to advance funds, the Master Servicer may terminate the Servicer", saying nothing about consent. Whether the proviso dispenses with the Note Insurer's consent is a conflict inside the provision's own words.

Reimbursement is allowed "from the Master Servicer Collection Account as Extraordinary Trust Fund Expenses", a category this Agreement does not define and which sits against the withdrawal provisions of Article V governing that account. Whether such costs may in fact be withdrawn ahead of Noteholders depends on those permitted-withdrawal provisions.

"The Master Servicer shall require the Servicer to comply" states a duty with no stated means or standard of performance, unlike Section 4.02(b), which spells out enforcement to the extent it "would require were it the owner of the HELOCs". What compliance the Master Servicer must actually secure is unmeasured.

The disclaimer that the Master Servicer "will not assume liability for the representations and warranties of the Servicer it replaces" leaves unaddressed whether it assumes the Servicer's ongoing servicing obligations, which Section 4.02(b) contemplates it performing on termination. The line between assumed duties and disclaimed warranties has to be drawn from the two subsections together.

The self-insurance alternative applies if LaSalle Bank "maintains with any Rating Agency the equivalent of a long term unsecured debt rating of 'A'", which does not say whose scale or what counts as an equivalent, and the required bond must be "in such form and amount generally acceptable for entities serving as master servicers or trustees". Neither standard has a determinable content.

Section 4.04 grants the Master Servicer "full power and authority to do any and all things that it may deem necessary or desirable" over the HELOCs, duplicating and partly overlapping the identical grant and the powers-of-attorney duty in Section 4.01, which imposes no Servicing Officer request requirement. Which section's conditions attach to the exercise of these powers cannot be settled from one alone.

The section says only that on an assumption "the original Mortgagor may be released from liability in accordance with the Servicing Agreement", without saying who exercises that permission or on what conditions. "To the extent HELOCs contain enforceable due-on-sale clauses" likewise supplies no test of enforceability.

The payoff certification must state that amounts were deposited in "the Protected Account maintained by the Servicer pursuant to the Servicing Agreement", while Section 2.01(e)(iii) requires the same kind of certificate to speak to "the related Collection Account" and Sections 2.02-2.04 route repurchase funds to the Master Servicer Collection Account. Which account governs the certification cannot be told from this subsection alone.

The final sentence provides that the Mortgage File must be returned when the need no longer exists "unless the related HELOC shall be liquidated, in which case ... the Mortgage File shall be released by the Indenture Trustee or the Custodian to the Servicer or the Master Servicer" — that is, on liquidation the file is released again rather than returned. The exception contradicts the obligation it qualifies.

This subsection requires access to HELOC information and documentation to be "afforded without charge", which cannot be squared with Section 4.01, which affords the same access to records and photocopying "at a charge that covers the Master Servicer, Securities Administrator and Indenture Trustee's actual costs". Which regime applies to a given request is left to construction.

The sentence runs "shall be held by the Master Servicer for and on behalf of the Issuing Entity, the Indenture Trustee, the Noteholders and the Certificateholders shall be and remain the sole and exclusive property of the Issuing Entity", omitting the conjunction and leaving two predicates joined without punctuation. Whether the funds are held for four beneficiaries or owned solely by the Issuing Entity turns on repairing that sentence.

The clause that "no earthquake or other additional insurance is to be required" pairs one specific peril with an open-ended catch-all, leaving unclear which coverages beyond fire, casualty and flood are excluded. The exception for "such applicable laws and regulations as shall at any time be in force" gives the catch-all no fixed boundary.

The subsection directs deposits into the Master Servicer Collection Account "pursuant to Sections 5.04 and 5.05" and withdrawals "pursuant to Sections 5.05 and 5.06", but under this Agreement's own table of contents Section 5.02 is the Master Servicer Collection Account and Section 5.03 its permitted withdrawals, while 5.04 and 5.05 govern the Payment Account. The cited sections do not do what the text says they do.

"Insurance Policies" is used here for policies on which claims are presented and recoveries realized, but the same defined term appears in Section 2.01(a)(iii) as the Originator's rights conveyed to the Trust, and Exhibit F to this Agreement is a "Form of Insurance Policy" for the Note Insurer's financial guaranty. Whether the Master Servicer's claims duty covers hazard policies, the guaranty policy, or both is not resolved by the words used.
